subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in user-output permission policy, and exactly which write surfaces and modes may it control without weakening private state?
rationale: The request is valid but changes local filesystem access boundaries and adds config surface, so automation should not choose the permanent security/product contract.

options.title: Design scoped user-output policy
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in policy for user-facing output only, with schema/docs/tests proving private state remains 0600/0700.

options.title: Fix only narrow permission bugs
options.body: Keep this broader feature open or deferred while handling specific reports such as outbound media and private state-directory hardening separately.

options.title: Reject core config knob
options.body: Document host ACL, Docker user/group, or deployment-level umask guidance and do not add a core permission policy.

recommendation.title: Design scoped user-output policy
recommendation.body: Add an explicit opt-in policy for user-facing output only, with schema/docs/tests proving private state remains 0600/0700.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on the central agent, sandbox mutation, and config-schema files that would define the boundary.
